hints: Focus on what counts as a sigma bond, remember every single bond is one sigma, while a double bond and a triple bond each contain only one sigma.
Expand the condensed formula first, the backbone has H-C, C-C, C-C, C=C, C-H plus two C-CH3 links, and each CH3 adds three C-H sigmas.
Add them systematically, count the 5 C-C backbone sigmas, then add all the C-H sigmas from the terminal H, the =CH and the two methyl groups to get the total.
walkthrough:
**Recall the sigma rule for multiple bonds**

Every bond, single, double or triple, contains exactly one sigma bond. Any extra bonds are pi bonds.

$$\text{single = 1 } \sigma, \quad \text{double = 1 } \sigma + 1 \pi, \quad \text{triple = 1 } \sigma + 2 \pi$$

**Draw out the skeleton**

Write the molecule as $\text{H}-\text{C} \equiv \text{C}-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)$. Label the four main carbons C1 to C4 from left to right.

$$\text{H}-\text{C1} \equiv \text{C2}-\text{C3}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C4H}(\text{CH}_3)$$

**Count sigma bonds on the backbone**

Now count one sigma for each connection you see. H-C1 is 1, C1 triple C2 is 1, C2-C3 is 1, C3 double C4 is 1, C4-H is 1, plus C3 to its $\text{CH}_3$ is 1 and C4 to its $\text{CH}_3$ is 1. That gives 7 sigma bonds in the framework.

**Add the methyl C-H bonds**

Each $\text{CH}_3$ group has 3 C-H single bonds, so 3 sigmas. With two methyl groups that is $2 \times 3 = 6$ sigmas.

$$7 \text{ (framework) } + 6 \text{ (methyl C-H) } = 13 \text{ } \sigma \text{ bonds}$$

options.A: 5 counts only the C-C sigma bonds (C1-C2, C2-C3, C3-CH3, C3=C4, C4-CH3). It forgets all the C-H sigma bonds, which are the majority in this hydrocarbon.
options.B: 11 is two short. It usually comes from miscounting hydrogens, for example forgetting the terminal H-C triple bond hydrogen and the =C-H hydrogen, or counting each CH3 as only 2 C-H bonds.
options.C: 13 is correct. There are 7 framework sigmas plus 6 C-H sigmas from the two CH3 groups, giving 13 sigma bonds in total. The 3 extra pi bonds (2 in the triple, 1 in the double) are not counted.
options.D: 16 counts every bond, sigma plus pi. The triple bond contributes 2 pi and the double bond contributes 1 pi, so 13 sigma + 3 pi = 16 total covalent bonds. The question asks for sigma only.
